correctness.rationale: For any two distinct words, pair distance <4 is equivalent to XOR support in a single adjacent cyclic two-set. Six four-bit erasure projections therefore must all be bijective on a 16-word code. Exhaustive exact-cover recursion over 96 requirements found 76 solutions (685 nodes), while independent pair-distance compatibility clique recursion found the same 76 sorted sixteen-word sets (391978 nodes). Every code was directly pair-distance checked, affinity and all 768 isometries were checked; five orbit sizes sum to 76. Search invariants prove completeness of finite domains.

value.rationale: The original literature motivated optimal read-pair codes; here (6,16,4) is a natural exact Singleton-equality case for recovery from two adjacent erasures. The bound and known constructions do not identify 32 genuinely nonaffine optimum designs, five isometry classes, or all 76 labeled choices. The exact reproducible finite classification provides a canonical design inventory and a structural boundary for linear-only constructions, not merely a new numerical bound or a routine re-expression of existence.
